clue.text: Sweet variety, cold in the middle

indicators.note: the cold letter is placed in the middle of the word for variety

parts.note: a variety on offer is a choice
C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A range of sweets is described as chilly at its centre.
explanation.walkthrough: A CHOC ICE is a British ice-cream bar coated in chocolate, here the 'sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate-coated ice-cream bar is a dessert or treat, so it counts as a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Sound, selfless injunction to physician

indicators.note: read as self-less, telling the solver to drop the word self from the saying

parts.note: the biblical proverb from Luke 4:23 is 'Physician, heal thyself'

explanation.surface: A clue about a doctor being told, altruistically, to stay well.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'Physician, heal thyself' is the injunction; 'selfless' strips SELF from THYSELF, leaving HEAL THY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound in body means in good health, the adjective sense of a robust constitution.

clue.text: Genetic information obtained from false leg

parts.note: cod is an informal adjective meaning fake or mock
in cricket the leg side is also called the on side

explanation.surface: A gene fact said to come from an artificial limb.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side of the field is also called the on side, so leg gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A codon is a triplet of nucleotides encoding one amino acid, a unit of genetic code.

clue.text: Monk spies retreating tank

indicators.note: the spies withdraw, so their letters leave the word for the monk

parts.note: a Cistercian is a monk of the order founded at Citeaux
the CIA is the American intelligence agency

explanation.surface: A monk catches sight of a tank backing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spies' looks like a verb; it is the CIA, which leaves CISTERCIAN to give CISTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a water storage container, a tank as found above a lavatory or in a loft.

clue.text: Initially inauspicious cloud has silver lining for poet

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word inauspicious is used
the silver sits inside the cloud as its lining, as in the proverb

parts.note: mist is a low cloud
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: An unpromising cloud with a silver lining inspires a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on the proverb that every cloud has a silver lining, taken literally here; Imagism was a movement of poets such as Ezra Pound.
explanation.definitionFit: An Imagist was a member of the early-twentieth-century poetry movement led by Pound and others.

clue.text: Regularly overlooked, our town is south of Maidenhead, Berks

indicators.note: in a down entry the second piece sits below the first

parts.note: the head of the word Maiden is its first letter

indicators.note: every other letter of the phrase is skipped over, keeping the odd ones

explanation.surface: A local claims their town lies south of Maidenhead in Berkshire.
explanation.walkthrough: Berks looks like the county abbreviation for Berkshire; here it is the plural of berk, British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Berk is British slang for an idiot, so berks are fools or dimwits.

clue.text: Articulating demand that Blair resign for blunder

indicators.note: the words are spoken, so their sound gives the letters

parts.note: telling Cherie Blair, wife of the former Prime Minister, to quit: 'Go, Cherie!'

explanation.surface: A call for a prime minister's departure is called a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: Blair here is Cherie Blair, wife of Tony Blair; 'Go, Cherie' spoken gives GAUCHERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaucherie is socially awkward behaviour or a tactless act, a faux pas or gaffe.

clue.text: Plastic capsule, which may be inserted into orifices

definitions.text: which may be inserted into orifices

indicators.note: plastic means mouldable, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A plastic pill casing meant for insertion into bodily openings.
explanation.definitionFit: Specula are medical instruments used to widen body openings for examination.

clue.text: Squealed as elephant's bits stirred

indicators.note: stirred means mixed up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and all letters are used

explanation.surface: An elephant's parts get mixed up, prompting squealing.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeal is slang for informing, revealing a secret, as does the idiom for blabbing.

clue.text: Howled out loud, having lost hair

indicators.note: the word is said, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: bawled means cried or howled loudly

explanation.surface: Someone cried noisily after losing their hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with no hair on the scalp is described as bald.

clue.text: Marvellous Madoff?

definitions.meaning: informal word for wonderful or excellent
Bernard Madoff ran a giant Ponzi scheme, so he was a ..., an outstanding cheat

explanation.walkthrough: A duper is one who dupes; Madoff was a superlative one.
explanation.definitionFit: Read one way it is gushing slang for excellent; read the other, an exceptional swindler.

clue.text: Instantly high-octane

indicators.note: high as in intoxicated, so the letters are tipsy and rearranged

explanation.surface: A two-word clue suggests a fuel of high octane rating acts immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means immediately, without any delay, the same as instantly.

clue.text: Yearn to take extended trip

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn
a haul is a catch or take, as of fish or loot

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to go on a lengthy journey.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-haul journey is one over a great distance, such as an intercontinental flight.

clue.text: Transform an annoying person into a B-lister?

definitions.text: Transform an annoying person into a B-lister?

parts.words: Transform an annoying person into a B-lister?
parts.note: a blister is an annoying person; adding a dash turns the word into B-lister

explanation.surface: A plan to demote an irritating celebrity to minor fame.
explanation.walkthrough: Blister is slang for a pest; adding a dash after the B gives B-lister.
explanation.definitionFit: To add a dash between parts of a word is to join or divide it with that punctuation mark.

clue.text: Unmoved, as I was after visiting San Francisco?

definitions.text: as I was after visiting San Francisco?
definitions.meaning: the song 'I Left My Heart in San Francisco' implies the singer came away without one

explanation.walkthrough: The allusion is to Tony Bennett's song 'I Left My Heart in San Francisco'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without compassion or pity means being cold and unmoved by others' suffering.

clue.text: Disclose opportunity to stop working

definitions.meaning: to make news known, as in reporting a story
a pause or rest period from work

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is revealing news; the other is a pause or rest from labour.

clue.text: Attempt to report Brownshirts

indicators.note: a report is a spoken account, so the letter names are said

parts.note: the SA, or Sturmabteilung, were the Nazi stormtroopers called Brownshirts

explanation.surface: An effort to inform on Nazi stormtroopers.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters SA said as names, 'ess-ay', give the word.
explanation.definitionFit: An essay is an old literary word for a try or effort, also as a verb.

clue.text: She wanders away from Rex, boring chap who goes on and on

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so the king's letter goes inside

parts.words: chap who goes on and on
parts.note: a stayer is someone with stamina who keeps going
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A woman flees from a tedious man named Rex who never stops talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring chap who goes on and on' reads as a tedious talker; 'boring' is the insertion and the chap is a stayer.
explanation.definitionFit: One who wanders off or roams from where she should be is a stray, a wanderer.

clue.text: Two English animals on the loose in Pacific region

indicators.note: loose animals are scattered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English, here taken twice

explanation.surface: A couple of English creatures escape in the South Seas.
explanation.definitionFit: Melanesia is the island group of the south-west Pacific including Fiji and Papua New Guinea.

clue.text: Diplomat's encouragement of revolutionary?

parts.note: atta, as in attaboy or attagirl, is a cry of encouragement
Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary

explanation.surface: An envoy's cheering on of a rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atta' is the encouraging cry from 'attaboy', here addressed to Che.
explanation.definitionFit: An attache is an embassy official, a member of a diplomatic staff.

clue.text: Altogether fascinated by muscle reflex

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

indicators.note: reflex means bent back, so the muscle word is read backwards

parts.note: lat is short for latissimus dorsi, a back muscle

explanation.surface: Someone is completely absorbed by a muscular reflex.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means as a sum, counting everything, the same as altogether.

clue.text: Removing meat from menu, serves exceptional seafood

indicators.note: the meat is the inner part of each word, so only its ends remain

explanation.surface: A restaurant drops meat dishes and offers excellent fish instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meat' is the middle of each word; taking it out leaves MU, SS and EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A mussel is an edible bivalve shellfish, a type of seafood.

clue.text: Beetle having quiet time in steaming ordure

parts.note: p is the musical marking piano, meaning quiet

indicators.note: the time letter goes inside the jumbled dung
steaming suggests agitation, so the letters are churned

explanation.surface: An insect is pictured silently waiting in a hot pile of dung.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' looks like the insect (a dung beetle fits) but is the verb meaning to jut out; 'steaming' turns ORDURE into ROURDE, which takes T.
explanation.definitionFit: Beetling brows overhang, so to beetle means to project or jut out.

clue.text: Makes fun of relative wearing trousers inside out

indicators.note: the relative is put on inside the trouser letters
the inside of the word is out, so only its ends stay

parts.note: an aunt is a family relative

explanation.surface: A family member wears trousers turned inside out and is mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: To taunt is to jeer at or mock someone provocatively.

clue.text: Ban is such as to make one fearful

definitions.meaning: Ban Ki-moon was Secretary-General of the United Nations
to deprive a person of courage or nerve

explanation.walkthrough: Ban Ki-moon headed the United Nations, so he is a 'UN man'.
explanation.definitionFit: To unman someone is to sap their courage, leaving them frightened or weak.

clue.text: Bitchy person I could strangle very fast

indicators.note: the words grip the answer within them as if throttling it

explanation.surface: Someone says a spiteful person is one they could throttle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypersonic describes speed above five times that of sound, far beyond supersonic.

clue.text: Half of mild, ten Navy Cut and a tot

indicators.note: only the first two of the four letters of the word mild are kept
the navy letter is removed from the number

explanation.surface: A list of tobacco and drink: mild ale, Navy Cut, and a dram.
explanation.walkthrough: Navy Cut is a brand of pipe tobacco and mild a beer, so the surface reads as pub orders; 'a tot' is a small child.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is a small child, a little one, just as a tot is.

clue.text: Doctor lays out basis of treatment and cure

indicators.note: out means wrongly arranged, so the letters are mixed
the basis is the beginning or foundation, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A doctor sets out a course of treatment and remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cure' looks medical with doctor and treatment, but means preserving food with salt.
explanation.definitionFit: To cure meat or fish is to preserve it, and drying with salt is one such method.

clue.text: Holiday home for setters?

parts.note: setters are breeds of dog, and boarding places look after dogs while owners are away

explanation.surface: A getaway cottage for crossword compilers.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters reads as crossword compilers; it means the dog breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Boarding establishments for dogs house them while their owners are on vacation.
